conclusion: Control of the Support Services transfers over time: the services are provided throughout each calendar month and the customer simultaneously receives and consumes their benefit as the Supplier provides them (CON-X02-T1), meeting paragraph 35(a), so each month's Monthly Fee is recognised as that month's services are provided. Clause 6.1 (CON-X02-T3) lets the customer claim a credit of 10% of the Monthly Fee when a Priority 1 request is not answered within 4 business hours, a credit that depends on a future event and makes the consideration variable; the fee is invoiced on or about the 17th of each month and is due within 14 days (CON-X02-T2).

reasoning_chain.text: Clause 4.1 (CON-X02-T1): the Support Services are provided throughout each calendar month, and the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit of the Support Services as the Supplier provides them.
Clause 6.1 (CON-X02-T3): if the Supplier does not respond to a Priority 1 request within 4 business hours, the customer may claim a credit of 10% of the Monthly Fee for that month.
Clause 5.1 and 5.2 (CON-X02-T2): the Monthly Fee for each calendar month is invoiced on or about the 17th day of that month and is payable within 14 days.
Revenue is recognised when (or as) the customer obtains control of the promised good or service (AASB 15 para 31).
Control transfers over time if the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits provided by the entity's performance as the entity performs (AASB 15 para 35(a)).
The customer receives and consumes the benefit of the support as it is provided, so paragraph 35(a) is met and control transfers over time, month by month.

The service-level credit arises only if a Priority 1 request is answered late in a month, a future event, so the consideration is variable; it may reduce that month's fee but does not change how control transfers.
Each month's Monthly Fee is recognised over that month as the support is provided, whatever the invoice date; the clause 6.1 credit is the only term that may reduce it.

counter_argument: A term requiring the customer to sign off each month's services before they count as provided would make that acceptance the transfer event instead.
